An IPv4 datagram carrying 4000 bytes of data (plus 20 bytes IP header) passes through a link with MTU = 1500 bytes. What is the fragment offset value in the second fragment?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
MTU = 1500 bytes. With 20-byte IP header, max payload per fragment is 1480 bytes (which is divisible by 8: $1480 / 8 = 185$).
- First fragment carries data bytes 0 to 1479 (offset = 0).
- Second fragment carries data starting at byte 1480. Fragment offset $= 1480 / 8 = 185$.

Consider yourself an engineer who wants to design a greedy algorithm for a tour company.

The tour company will be given a list of nn tourists, each with a positive minimum hotel space requirement s1,…,sn.s1,…,sn.

The tour company will also have a list of mm available hotel rooms with each room RjRj having an area ajaj and a price pj.pj.

Assume hotel has enough rooms i.e. m>nm>n.

The company wants to assign each tourist ii a distinct room such that area of the assigned room ≥si.≥si.

Consider two strategies below. As an engineer, decide that which strategy will allot rooms to tourists such that the total price can be minimized.

Greedy strategy A:Greedy strategy A: Take the tourist with the smallest space requirement. Assign that tourist the cheapest room that meets the requirement. Remove that tourist and the assigned room and repeat until all tourists are assigned rooms. (If no such room exists, output "no legal assignments").

Greedy strategy B:Greedy strategy B: Take the tourist with the largest space requirement. Assign that tourist the cheapest room that meets the requirement. Remove that tourist and the assigned room and repeat until all tourists are assigned rooms. (If no such room exists, output “no legal assignments”).

The optimal solution is a solution that minimizes the total price for the tour companies.
